body.statement: Assume \(S\) is realizable. Every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\) satisfies \(\operatorname{supp}(\theta_j)\subseteq T_j(S)\) for all \(j\). Every \(r\in T(S)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(r)\in S\), and \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(T(S))=S\). Consequently, every product law strictly positive on each \(T_j(S)\) has factual support exactly \(S\), and \(T(S)\) is the unique largest Cartesian response support among all members of \(\Theta_S\).
body.justification: This removes chart ambiguity before any identifying formula is constructed.
body.gap: Zaffalon et al. give local credal constraints and Chen and Darwiche prune zero circuit branches, but neither proves query-independent sufficiency and uniqueness of this support saturation.
body.consumer: The maximal chart is the finite domain on which the tensor identifier and every nonidentification witness are certified.
body.proof_tex:
For \(\theta\in\Theta_S\), put \(A_j=\operatorname{supp}(\theta_j)\).  For a prefix \(w\in\prod_{\ell=1}^k\mathcal X_\ell\), define, only within this proof,
\[
q_j^k(w)=\sum_{r_j\in\mathcal R_j}\theta_j(r_j)b_j^k(w,r_j).
\]
The indicator of the event \(\{\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(r)_{\le k}=w\}\) is
\[
\prod_{j=1}^m b_j^k(w,r_j).
\]
Indeed, by acyclicity and the topological order, the prefix is \(w\) exactly when every response equation whose vertex occurs by time \(k\) returns the corresponding coordinate of \(w\); the factors in \(b_j^k\) partition these equations by district.  The product root law in the definition of \(\theta\) therefore gives the prefix factorization
\[
P_\theta(V_{\le k}=w)
=\sum_{r}\prod_{j=1}^m\theta_j(r_j)b_j^k(w,r_j)
=\prod_{j=1}^m q_j^k(w).                                      \tag{1}
\]

Fix \(i\), let \(V_i\in D_j\), and take \((w,a)\in\mathcal F_i(S)\).  Since \(w\in S^{\le i-1}\), there is an \(s\in S\) extending \(w\).  Exact support, as encoded by \(\theta\in\Theta_S\), gives
\[
P_\theta(V_{<i}=w)\ge P_\theta(s)>0.
\]
Equation (1), whose factors are nonnegative, consequently implies \(q_\ell^{i-1}(w)>0\) for every \(\ell\).  For \(\ell\ne j\), no response equation from district \(D_\ell\) is added at step \(i\), and hence
\[
b_\ell^i(wa,r_\ell)=b_\ell^{i-1}(w,r_\ell),
\qquad
q_\ell^i(wa)=q_\ell^{i-1}(w)>0.                                \tag{2}
\]
On the other hand, \(wa\notin S^{\le i}\), so exact support and (1)--(2) give
\[
0=P_\theta(V_{\le i}=wa)
=q_j^i(wa)\prod_{\ell\ne j}q_\ell^{i-1}(w),
\qquad q_j^i(wa)=0.                                             \tag{3}
\]
Every summand in the definition of \(q_j^i\) is nonnegative.  Thus (3) and \(\theta_j(r_j)>0\) for \(r_j\in A_j\) imply
\[
b_j^i(wa,r_j)=0
\quad\hbox{for every }r_j\in A_j.
\]
Since this holds for every first forbidden extension belonging to district \(D_j\), the definition of \(T_j(S)\) yields
\[
A_j\subseteq T_j(S)\qquad(j=1,\ldots,m).                       \tag{4}
\]

Now take any \(r\in T(S)\), and write \(v=\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(r)\).  Suppose that \(v\notin S\).  Since \(S^{\le0}=\{()\}\), there is a least \(i\) for which \(v_{\le i}\notin S^{\le i}\).  Then \(v_{<i}\in S^{\le i-1}\), so \((v_{<i},v_i)\in\mathcal F_i(S)\).  If \(V_i\in D_j\), factual evaluation of \(r\) along its own prefix makes every factor in \(b_j^i(v_{\le i},r_j)\) equal to one.  Hence
\[
b_j^i(v_{\le i},r_j)=1,
\]
contrary to \(r_j\in T_j(S)\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(T(S))\subseteq S.              \tag{5}
\]

By realizability there is \(\theta^\star\in\Theta_S\).  For each \(s\in S\), the finite sum defining \(P_{\theta^\star}(s)>0\) contains a tuple \(r\) with \(\prod_j\theta_j^\star(r_j)>0\) and \(\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(r)=s\).  Such a tuple belongs to \(\prod_j A_j^\star\), which is contained in \(T(S)\) by (4).  Thus \(S\subseteq\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(T(S))\), and together with (5) this proves
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{\varnothing}(T(S))=S.                       \tag{6}
\]

Let \(\eta_j\) be any mass function strictly positive at every element of \(T_j(S)\), extended by zero to \(\mathcal R_j\setminus T_j(S)\).  Realizability and (4) ensure that every \(T_j(S)\) is nonempty.  Under \(\bigotimes_j\eta_j\), every tuple in \(T(S)\) has positive probability.  Its pushforward support is therefore exactly the image in (6), namely \(S\).  Hence this product law belongs to \(\Theta_S\).  Finally, the response support of any member of \(\Theta_S\) is the Cartesian set \(\prod_j A_j\), and (4) places it inside \(T(S)\), whereas the preceding strictly positive law has response support equal to \(T(S)\).  Thus \(T(S)\) is the unique largest Cartesian response support.
